clue.text: Die in the cooler?

parts.note: a die is a small cube, and one sitting in the fridge or cool box would be frozen water shaped that way

explanation.surface: Reads like a question about someone expiring in prison, 'the cooler' being slang for jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' wants to be the verb and 'cooler' a prison; instead the die is the cube-shaped thing you roll, and the cooler keeps drinks cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling die is a small cube, so a frozen block from the freezer tray is a die in the cooler.

clue.text: See 19
Off-white stuff, single or double ultimately consumed

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to stuff is to cram, packing something in tight

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word double (single ends the same way)

explanation.surface: Talks of the off-white dairy product, single or double, finally being eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single or double' prompts the dairy sense, but either word ends in E, which goes inside CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is a pale yellowish-white colour name, a shade slightly off pure white.

clue.text: In young feline one head lifts, with swollen nodes

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the whole assembly turns it so it reads from bottom to top
In places the following pieces inside the young feline

parts.note: a cub is a young lion or tiger
one is the Roman numeral I
nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Pictures a lion cub raising its head, followed by a medical aside about swollen glands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head lifts' seems to act on the head alone, but 'lifts' turns the whole assembly (CINOBUB) upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubonic plague is marked by buboes, the painfully swollen lymph glands, so the adjective describes that condition.

clue.text: Something useful I agree — it has practicality in the end

parts.note: amen is said to express assent, so it is an 'I agree'
taken as written

indicators.note: in the end picks out the final letter of practicality

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing that a handy thing is, at bottom, practical.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility such as a pool or shop is a convenience that makes a place more pleasant or useful.

clue.text: Church fairly dismisses it, after reduction in the majority

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed fairly word behind the trimmed majority word
a reduction trims the word for majority by one letter at its tail

parts.note: the majority is most of it

indicators.note: dismisses means the second word is sent out of the first

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in quite good
the word it is removed as written

explanation.surface: A church sending something away once most of it has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church' looks like a Christian building, but any house of worship serves; 'dismisses it' drops those two letters literally, and 'reduction' docks only a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque is a Muslim place of worship, so it stands loosely for a church in the general sense of a house of prayer.

clue.text: Uncompromising leader breaking ground no more, UN chief

indicators.note: breaking means the letter forces its way into the middle of the other letters
ground, as in milled, means these letters are crushed and rearranged
leader takes the first letter of Uncompromising

explanation.surface: A hardline UN chief who will break no more ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncompromising leader' reads as one person but gives only U; 'chief' at the end is the definition, not part of 'UN chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for number one, this phrase is used in English for the top person or boss.

clue.text: Audibly, don't eat in Yorkshire? Don't listen!

indicators.note: Audibly says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'nowt' means nothing, so 'chew nowt' is don't eat

explanation.surface: A dialect instruction not to eat, followed by a cry of not wanting to hear any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chew nowt' (Yorkshire dialect, 'nowt' meaning nothing) spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop paying attention or ignore what is being said is a phrasal verb meaning to stop listening.

clue.text: Wheel round new cornet and drum finally, for top musician

indicators.note: round means the wheel word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a caster is a small swivelling wheel on furniture

indicators.note: new means the letters of cornet are made into a fresh arrangement
finally takes the last letter of drum

explanation.surface: Instruments wheeled around for the leading player of an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel round' reads as a verb phrase, but 'Wheel' is a noun for a furniture castor and 'round' is the container; 'new' rearranges cornet to ONCERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of an orchestra's first violins, chief among its players, is called this in American usage.

clue.text: See 28
Doing well to disperse Lisbon smog

indicators.note: to disperse is to scatter, so the letters of Lisbon smog are spread out anew

explanation.surface: A city thriving once its smog clears away.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourishing person or business is thriving, like a plant coming into flower.

clue.text: Poles securing harmless part of a flowering plant

indicators.note: securing means the poles hold the other word safe between them

parts.note: S and N are the abbreviations for the south and north poles
a tame animal is harmless

explanation.surface: Poles staked to hold up a harmless piece of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing male organ of a flower, with its filament and anther, is a botanical component.

clue.text: Brush on odd bits of colour where social events held

indicators.note: on puts the brush word after the colour letters
odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters of colour

parts.note: a broom is a long-handled brush

explanation.surface: Applying daubs of colour with a brush, as if decorating a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A room used by a society's members for meetings and gatherings is a venue for its functions.

clue.text: Advantage held by business tycoon, bounder about right!

parts.note: Donald Trump is a property tycoon

indicators.note: about means the cad goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, an ill-mannered man

explanation.surface: A tycoon holding an edge, decried as a bounder.
explanation.definitionFit: A key resource kept back to win the day, like a card of the winning suit, is an edge or advantage.

clue.text: Fruit, one of seven on top of two lockers

indicators.note: in a down light, on top of puts the day above the lockers

parts.note: Monday, shortened to Mon, is one of the seven days of the week
a key locks a door and a nut locks onto a bolt
a key locks a door and a nut locks onto a bolt

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which of seven things sits on two lockers.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut is called this in Britain; botanically it is a seed pod, loosely a fruit.

clue.text: Capital with 6, you could say, bringing 18

definitions.meaning: 6 is a place of worship pronounced 'mosk'; said together with this word it sounds like the insect that carries 18, malaria

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing riddle linking a city, a place of worship and a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 6-down's answer said in front of this word makes the name of the insect that spreads 18-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ecuadorian seat of government, high in the Andes, is a national capital city.

clue.text: Asian home, a second knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: in means at home
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A house knocked down in a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Gulf sultanate in the Arabian peninsula is an Asian national.

clue.text: Killer song, a hit written up

indicators.note: in a down light, written up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: A deadly hit song, reviewed in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: This mosquito-borne tropical disease is among the world's deadliest, so it is a killer.

clue.text: Moving ship beyond wave, an up-and-down experience

indicators.note: beyond puts the ship after the wave

parts.note: moving means stirring the feelings
a roller is a big breaking wave
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A ship sailing past a wave, which sounds rough and up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a stretch of life with dramatic highs and lows, like a fairground ride.

clue.text: Raw pastry dish then cut, top sliced off

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with filling

indicators.note: top sliced off removes the first letter of the word for cut

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: a pastry dish, cut, its crust sliced off.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is served uncooked, so the culinary term describes raw meat.

clue.text: Space around middle of hole beginning to reduce, describing coloured rings

indicators.note: around means the space word goes round the letters from hole

parts.note: an area is a space

indicators.note: middle of takes the two central letters of hole
beginning to takes the first letter of reduce

explanation.surface: A gap around the centre of a hole starting to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to an areola, the ring of coloured skin around a nipple or similar circle.

clue.text: Among maestri, one raised towards the heavens as an artist

indicators.note: in a down light, heading towards the heavens means reading upwards
Among says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: One of the great masters lifted up to heaven, as an artist might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste is the French Impressionist painter famed for sunlit scenes, so the surname names an artist.

clue.text: Compared with a crossword, Sudoku is so idiotic

definitions.text: Compared with a crossword, Sudoku is so
definitions.meaning: a Sudoku comes with numbers only and no written hints, unlike a crossword

explanation.surface: A grumble that number puzzles are mindless next to word puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly without a clue is stupid or witless, which fits idiotic.

clue.text: See 19
Easy crossword solution

definitions.meaning: not hard or heavy, as easy work
in setters' jargon, each answer entered in the grid is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Easy work is undemanding, and puzzle makers call each grid entry by the same word.

clue.text: Big performance one feeling someone must grasp and then appreciate, primarily

indicators.note: must grasp means the groper holds the next word inside

parts.note: a groper is one who feels someone up
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of appreciate

explanation.surface: A grand show where one sensitive person must take things in and appreciate them.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale serious opera, sung throughout with full orchestra, is a big stage production.

clue.text: Sport to sell that's backfired

indicators.note: backfired suggests going into reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to flog is to sell

explanation.surface: A sports marketing campaign that went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The club-and-ball game played over a course of holes is a sport.

clue.text: Where Port Elizabeth is a pretence, as liberal

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A political charge that someone's liberalism is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Elizabeth is a coastal city in South Africa; 'liberal' looks political but rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African province on the south-east coast contains the port city once called Port Elizabeth.

clue.text: News agency reporting writers from the Midlands?

indicators.note: reporting suggests speech, so the word is judged by sound

parts.note: in a Birmingham or Black Country accent, writers comes out as 'roiters'

explanation.surface: Journalists from central England working for a news agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is central England; its accent turns 'writers' into something like 'roiters'.
explanation.definitionFit: The London-founded international wire service supplies stories to newspapers worldwide.
